newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli fraud squad questions Netanyahu attorney.
newsitem.headline: Israeli fraud squad questions Netanyahu attorney.

text.p: Israel's police fraud squad questioned an Israeli peacemaker who is also Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's lawyer on Tuesday about alleged corruption in the appointment of an attorney-general.

"What I can tell you is that I came here to fulfill my civic duty to give testimony. What can I do?" the attorney, Yitzhak Molho, told reporters before entering the national fraud squad offices in Jaffa near Tel Aviv.

Molho helped negotiate Israel's handover to the PLO of most of the West Bank town of Hebron. He was one of three lawyers to be questioned, including Roni Bar-On, the man whose appointment by Netanyahu this month prompted the inquiry.
Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office, caught in a swirl of debate over charges he got the job more for his loyalty to Netanyahu's Likud party than his legal acumen.

A state-run television report then gave rise to charges the appointment was criminal as well as poor judgement. But Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told parliament's laws committee on Tuesday: "We still have no evidence."

On Sunday, police launched an inquiry into the Channel One television report that Bar-On's appointment was part of a deal with Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, a political kingmaker on trial for corruption since 1993.
It said Deri, an ultra-Orthodox Jew and ex-cabinet minister, demanded Bar-On get the job in return for Shas party support for Netanyahu's accord with the PLO on Hebron, completed this month.
The television said as part of the deal, Bar-On promised Deri a plea-bargain that would have let Deri continue his political career. The cabinet later approved the Hebron deal with Shas's support.

Netanyahu, in office only seven months, has denied the charges along with Bar-On and Deri. On Tuesday Bar-On said he had lodged a libel complaint against the television station's director-general, news director and correspondent.
